original_question: Is the regular order of contact of a smooth pseudoconvex domain the same as the commutator type, one vector field at a time.
target_in_paper: The supplied identifier arXiv:math/9509202 resolves to an unrelated problem list, not a paper containing Conjecture 1.1, Proposition 1.2, and Theorem 1.3 on contact/commutator type. Your draft nevertheless clearly matches the fixed-vector-field version of the Bloom/D'Angelo problem: for a smooth pseudoconvex real hypersurface, does the commutator type of a single nonzero tangential (1,0)-vector field equal the corresponding directional regular order of contact, equivalently the Levi type?
correct_elements: The draft correctly identifies the core comparison: regular order of contact versus commutator type, under smooth pseudoconvexity, and in the 'one vector field at a time' directional sense rather than the global supremum over all subbundles.
missing_details: The ambient space should be specified: a smooth real hypersurface M = b\Omega in \mathbb{C}^n (or a smooth pseudoconvex domain \Omega \subset \mathbb{C}^n with boundary M).
A boundary point p \in M must be fixed.
The question is directional: one fixes a germ of a smooth tangential (1,0) vector field L with L(p) \neq 0.
The 'regular order of contact' must mean the maximal order of contact at p of nonsingular holomorphic curves/disks tangent to the complex line \mathbb{C}L(p).
The commutator type t(L,p) must be defined as the least length of an iterated commutator in L and \overline{L} whose pairing with the contact form (or defining-form normal direction) is nonzero at p.
The Levi type c(L,p) must be defined as the least order at which a derivative in the directions L and \overline{L} of the Levi form in the direction L becomes nonzero at p.
It should be made explicit whether one is asking for t(L,p)=c(L,p), or directly for t(L,p) to equal the directional regular contact order; Proposition 1.2 is what supplies this equivalence.
The quantifiers are missing: the question is whether the equality holds for every smooth pseudoconvex boundary point p and every such L.
The draft says 'domain', but the invariant is really attached to the boundary hypersurface; this should be stated explicitly.
The smoothness class should be stated as C^\infty (or at least smooth) if one wants to match the standard formulation.
No homogeneity, degree restriction, nilpotency condition, or 'for all sufficiently large m' clause is relevant here; those should not be imported.
refined_question: Let \Omega \subset \mathbb{C}^n be a C^\infty-smooth pseudoconvex domain, let p \in b\Omega, and let L be a germ of a smooth tangential (1,0)-vector field on b\Omega with L(p) \neq 0. If t(L,p) denotes the commutator type of L at p (the smallest length of an iterated commutator of L and \overline{L} whose normal component at p is nonzero) and c(L,p) denotes the Levi type of L at p (the smallest order at which a derivative in the directions L and \overline{L} of the Levi form in the direction L is nonzero at p), must one always have t(L,p)=c(L,p)?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, via the paper's Proposition 1.2 reformulation, for every smooth pseudoconvex boundary point p and every nonzero tangential (1,0)-vector field L, is t(L,p) equal to the maximal order of contact at p of regular holomorphic curves through p whose tangent direction is the complex line \mathbb{C}L(p)?
justification: Your draft is close in spirit but not stand-alone. The directional phrase 'one vector field at a time' points away from the global Bloom conjecture over all s-dimensional subbundles and toward the fixed-field problem discussed in the literature on type. D'Angelo and Kohn explicitly define the single-field commutator type t(L,p) and the related Levi type c(L,p), note that the converse from directional commutator information to osculating complex curves is not true in general, and state that the pseudoconvex case is the expected one. Bloom's 1981 theorem gives the missing geometric side in the pseudoconvex C^3 setting by proving equality of regular contact type and Levi type; later expositions identify the remaining issue as whether the commutator type also agrees. Since the provided arXiv identifier is mismatched, the most paper-faithful refinement is the fixed-vector-field equality t(L,p)=c(L,p), together with its equivalent directional regular-contact formulation.
